name: Palmer
intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Palmer for 2026, and here is what he found: 5 family events, 1 of them free. The magic runs from November 26 (Bright Up the Night at the Alaska State Fairgrounds) through January 2, 2027 (the same drive-through lights), with The Christmas Factory (November 27 to December 23), Santa Experience Tours at Williams Reindeer Farm (December 5 to 20), Colony Christmas (December 11 to 13) and the Parade of Lights (December 12) along the way. We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.

What Rally found in Palmer

  • 5 Christmas events for kids in Palmer
  • 1 free event: the Colony Christmas Parade of Lights
  • Meet Santa: The Christmas Factory tour and the Santa Experience Tour at Williams Reindeer Farm
  • Lights and parades: Bright Up the Night drive-through lights (November 26 to January 2) and the Parade of Lights with fireworks (December 12)
  • Reindeer: Santa Experience Tour at Williams Reindeer Farm (December 5 to 20)
  • Season: November 26, 2026 to January 2, 2027

Planning a bigger day out? Palmer families also use our guide to Christmas activities for kids in Anchorage, which covers Zoo Lights and The Nutcracker with Eugene Ballet and more.

lede: Palmer turns its downtown into a Colony Christmas weekend with a parade of lights and fireworks, and the Alaska State Fairgrounds add a drive-through light show and a walk-through Christmas factory.
celebrates: The Greater Palmer Chamber of Commerce anchors the season with Colony Christmas, a weekend of festive cheer that its page says ends the big Saturday night with a Parade of Lights and fireworks over the Alaskan sky. Most stops are within walking distance of downtown, and a Mat-Su visitors blog lists decorated trees, gingerbread displays and Santa Claus himself. The Alaska State Fair runs Bright Up the Night, a drive-through display of more than 70 light installations, and The Christmas Factory, a family owned business, runs a guided elf tour on the fairgrounds. Williams Reindeer Farm adds guided Santa tours with reindeer.
lastyear: We did not find a full 2025 recap for Palmer, so this page relies on host descriptions. The Greater Palmer Chamber ran Colony Christmas in 2025, and a Mat-Su visitors blog post describes the weekend, listing December 12 to 14 for those dates. It says the Parade of Lights starts at 5 pm on Saturday, the Palmer Water Tower is lit at the same time, and fireworks follow about 15 minutes after the last float. Events continue on Sunday, according to that post.
facts: Palmer began as a New Deal experiment. The National Park Service says the Matanuska Colony was founded in 1935 and helped two hundred families, chosen by lot, settle in Alaska and get land for farming. The state's historic preservation office says the first colonists, from Minnesota, reached Palmer on May 10, 1935. The Alaska State Fairgrounds, home to Bright Up the Night and The Christmas Factory, sit in Palmer today.
trains: Palmer has no Christmas train ride on our 2026 list. The Alaska State Fair's Bright Up the Night is a drive-through light display, and The Christmas Factory is a walking tour with elves. For Santa trains and holiday rail rides elsewhere in Alaska, see our Alaska Christmas train rides guide, or check our Anchorage page for events a short drive south.
traditions: A weekend of downtown holiday events run by the Greater Palmer Chamber of Commerce.
A Saturday evening parade of floats decorated with holiday lights, followed by fireworks.
A drive-through display of more than 70 light installations at the Alaska State Fairgrounds.
A guided one hour elf tour with a bakery, toy room and Santa's office on the fairgrounds.
Guided Santa tours with reindeer at Williams Reindeer Farm on Bodenburg Loop.
kidfact: Palmer was founded in 1935 when about two hundred families came to farm the Matanuska Valley, and Colony Christmas ends with fireworks.
faq: Palmer's big weekend is Colony Christmas, run by the Greater Palmer Chamber of Commerce, with a Parade of Lights and fireworks on Saturday night and holiday stops around downtown. The Alaska State Fairgrounds add Bright Up the Night, a drive-through light display, and The Christmas Factory elf tour, and Williams Reindeer Farm offers Santa tours.
What is Colony Christmas in Palmer?

Colony Christmas is a weekend of holiday events in downtown Palmer organized by the Greater Palmer Chamber of Commerce. It features a Parade of Lights, fireworks, markets and community stops run by local businesses and groups. The chamber says it does not manage the individual community stops, so check each host.
Is there a drive-through Christmas lights show in Palmer?

Yes. The Alaska State Fair runs Bright Up the Night at the fairgrounds, a drive-through display of more than 70 light installations. Guests stay in their vehicles, and each ticket covers one vehicle and one visit. Gate prices are higher than online prices, so buy ahead if you can.
Can kids see reindeer and Santa in Palmer?

Yes. Williams Reindeer Farm on Bodenburg Loop offers a guided Santa Experience Tour with reindeer on select December dates, and the tours are outdoors. The Christmas Factory at the fairgrounds also includes a visit with Santa. Both book through online calendars, so reserve a time before you go.
Why is Palmer called a colony town?

Palmer was the center of the Matanuska Colony, a New Deal program that moved about two hundred families to the Matanuska Valley in 1935 to farm. The first colonists from Minnesota arrived in Palmer that May, according to Alaska state historians.
